items.q:
In a STAAD.Pro input file a support is written as:

SUPPORTS
1 PINNED

What does node 1 do under load?
options: Cannot move or rotate in any direction
Can rotate about Z only, moves freely in Y
Cannot move in X, Y or Z, but can rotate freely
Can move in X only, cannot rotate
items.explain: PINNED restrains all three translations and releases all three rotations, so no moment develops at that support.

items.q: A simply supported beam spans 6 m and carries a factored UDL of 20 kN/m (self weight included). What maximum bending moment MZ should the STAAD member output show?
items.explain: For a simply supported beam under UDL, Mmax = wL^2/8 = 20 x 36 / 8 = 90 kN.m at midspan; 60 kN is the end shear, not the moment.

items.q:
Load case 1 (DL) gives a column base reaction of 100 kN and load case 2 (LL) gives 60 kN.

LOAD COMB 3
1 1.5 2 1.5

What reaction does combination 3 report?
items.explain: A load combination scales and adds the primary results: 1.5 x 100 + 1.5 x 60 = 240 kN, which is the IS 456 limit state 1.5(DL + LL) case.

items.q: You add PDELTA ANALYSIS to a 10-storey frame. For the 1.2(DL + LL + EQ) case, should the loads be defined with LOAD COMB or REPEAT LOAD?
options: Neither, P-Delta needs a separate model
REPEAT LOAD, because P-Delta results cannot be added linearly
LOAD COMB, because it runs faster
items.explain: LOAD COMB only adds results of already-solved primary cases, so a nonlinear P-Delta analysis needs REPEAT LOAD, which re-solves the frame under the combined loads.

items.q:
With UNIT METER KN in force, a beam is given:

MEMBER PROPERTY
5 PRIS YD 0.45 ZD 0.3

What section has been defined?
options: 300 mm deep and 450 mm wide rectangle
450 mm deep and 300 mm wide rectangle
items.explain: For a PRIS rectangle YD is the depth along the local Y-axis (bending depth) and ZD the width, both in the current length unit, here metres.

items.q: Per IS 875 (Part 3), the design wind speed at a level works out to Vz = 40 m/s. What design wind pressure would you apply on the frame in STAAD?
items.explain: Design wind pressure pz = 0.6 Vz^2 = 0.6 x 1600 = 960 N/m2 = 0.96 kN/m2, which is then converted to member loads on the exposed frame.

items.q: A steel tie has gross area 1100 mm2, Fe 250 (fy = 250 N/mm2). Per IS 800, what is the design strength for yielding of the gross section (gamma_m0 = 1.10)?
items.explain: Tdg = Ag x fy / gamma_m0 = 1100 x 250 / 1.10 = 250,000 N = 250 kN; 275 kN forgets the partial safety factor.

items.q: You are running concrete design in STAAD with UNIT METER KN active. Which parameter line correctly sets M25 concrete?
items.explain: FC must be in the current stress unit, and 25 N/mm2 equals 25,000 kN/m2; entering FC 25 in kN/m2 would design for almost zero-strength concrete.

items.q:
The input contains:

MEMBER RELEASE
12 START MZ

What effect does this have on member 12?
options: No moment about Z at its start end (behaves as a hinge)
Its start node becomes fully fixed
Member 12 is removed from the analysis
Its start node cannot move in the Z direction
items.explain: A member release sets that end force to zero, so START MZ makes the start of the member behave like a pin for major-axis bending.

items.q: A 6 m simply supported beam carries a single point load of 60 kN at 2 m from the left support. What maximum MZ should the analysis output show?
items.explain: Left reaction = 60 x 4 / 6 = 40 kN, so Mmax under the load = 40 x 2 = 80 kN.m; 90 kN.m is the PL/4 value, which applies only for a midspan load.

items.q: Building in Zone III (Z = 0.16), I = 1.0, SMRF with R = 5, Sa/g = 2.5, seismic weight W = 5000 kN. Per IS 1893, what design base shear should your equivalent static load produce?
